A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Poisson midpoint sampling work. All 22 pages of each version, including Appendices A–H, are available and readable; text extraction and visual checks support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports convergence theorems and mathematical proofs, with no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes in the main text or appendices.

after.justification: v3 remains a theoretical paper. Its results and appendices contain mathematical guarantees and proofs, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The overdamped and underdamped PLMC update equations and randomized midpoint mechanism are retained. Corollaries 1 and 2 make a limited procedural refinement to batch-size selection, replacing the previous formulas with K proportional to max(ηL/ε², 1) and max(ηL/(ε√α), 1), respectively.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirically evaluated task scenarios. The theoretical strongly log-concave sampling problem and both Langevin variants are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Table 1 retains the same theoretical LMC, RLMC, and PLMC comparisons; its corrected assumption labels do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both versions lack empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, and experimental budgets. The revised batch-size prescriptions occur in theoretical convergence corollaries.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies. The appendix revisions concern mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The probabilistic moment and tail bounds are theoretical proof ingredients.

E6.justification: The complexity formulas and comparison rankings in Table 1 and Remarks 2 and 4 are unchanged. Neither version reports empirical result entries; revisions to mathematical conditions and derivations are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Corollaries 1 and 2 remove the small-ε restrictions associated with batch-size feasibility, with corresponding step-size inequality arguments in Appendices C.2 and F. v3 also corrects κ from L/µ to L/α, the extra Wasserstein-distance square in Appendix A.1, the missing η/K scaling of a term in Lemma 7's proof, and the iterate in Lemma 9's telescoping step. Theorem 3 specifies c0's dependence on p. These are localized refinements; the principal rates and proof strategy remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 2.4, and Section 7 retain the claims of cubic improvement in accuracy dependence over Euler–Maruyama, better accuracy dependence than existing randomized midpoint bounds, and Wasserstein sampling guarantees beyond strong-error lower bounds.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 corrects the applicability comparison from LSI being more general than log-concavity to being more general than strong log-concavity. Section 2.2 explicitly states computational cost's independence from K. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning dimension and condition-number dependence.

D1.justification: Corollaries 1 and 2 revise the concrete batch-size prescriptions, and Section 2.2 clarifies computational cost. The shared initialization now stated there was already used in v2's proofs. Neither version supplies code, hardware, or measured-runtime information.

R1.justification: The same 32 references and central research positioning remain. Table 1 corrects the assumptions attached to the non-LSI comparison bounds to strongly log-concave, and Section 2.3 corrects the relationship to LSI-based guarantees. These are limited scope corrections to the prior-work comparison.

P1.justification: v3 corrects grammar and terminology, revises short passages in Section 2.2, explains the role of p and the η-dependent remainder after Theorem 3, and standardizes reference-title capitalization. The main sections and Appendix A–H organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 widens its assumption columns and reduces the table's text size and height to accommodate 'Strongly Log-Concave'. Its two-panel structure remains. Other changes are localized equation and page reflow, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision and usability through corrected assumption labels, a consistent condition-number definition, repaired proof expressions, and batch-size prescriptions bounded below by one with corresponding appendix revisions. These changes make the existing analysis easier to apply and check. The core method, proof approach, and principal convergence-rate claims remain stable, so the overall gain is limited.
